title: Decapsulate
content: A podcast by Tris and Robin Last I looked there are only 7 episodes and I listened to them all over a couple of days. Reminded me a bit of the early years of Cortex without the podcasting machine that is Myke Hurley falling into interviewer mode. Also because of the RSI chat from Tris being reminiscent of CGP Grey's troubles. That being said the two key things I took from it are the ideas of Digital Gardening and Techno-Feudalism.

title: Digital Garden Home
content: Hello and welcome. Digital Gardening is a concept I personally came across on the Decapsulate podcast. I thought it sounded a nice thing to try for me; who much prefers indoor activities to real gardening and who struggles to "publish" things online due to a perfectionist mindset. This project will hopefully help me actively build out my thinking on certain topics and actually produce something for the outside world to see. All pages here are subject to change (and hopefully growth). Potential topics: Food and Science Productivity Research culture

title: Digital Gardening
content: A public space where notes grow, interlink, and are cultivated. Typically, the maturity of a note is shown through a borrowed nomenclature of seedlings through to evergreens. The idea (from what I can find) was developed by Maggie Appleton and you can see a walkthrough of the journey in her History & Ethos page in her garden. I see this as an opportunity not to have to produce a publication schedule or even coherently order the stuff I'm doing as the links rather than chronology does the work of building the garden. Found useful resources from Wanderloots (including how to set this up) and the discussions in the Decapsulate podcast. All obviously helped by the fact I have been using obsidian for years and love a productivity push.

title: Lost Terminal
content: I tried this podcast about a lonely satellite because I enjoy listening to Tris' voice. However, I can't say I was blown away by the pilot/first episode and I am yet to download any more.

title: Research culture
content: I am lucky to have been part of a movement at Oxford to try and better the research culture that has provided me with a number of unique experiences while trying to speak up for others. Most recently that takes the form of being a UK Research Staff Association representative on the Researcher Development Concordat Strategy Group led by Prof Richard Emes. In a meeting recently I was reminded of the a Taoist principle that the best leader helps in an invisible way such that when the work is done people say they did it themselves. Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing) Chapter 17 by Lao Tzu.
